He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia Lions]] and the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He was the [[2019–20 Ivy League men's basketball season|2019–20 Ivy League]] scoring champion. He has also led both the [[Ivy League]] (2017–18) and the [[Big Ten]] (2020–21) in assists per game. ==Early life== As an eighth-grader in 2012, Smith led Burr Ridge Middle School in [[Burr Ridge, Illinois]] to an [[Illinois Elementary School Association]] state championship.{{cite web |last1=Wilcox |first1=George M. |title=Nick Rakocevic, Mike Smith build on eighth-grade basketball success |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/elmhurst/sports/ct-dws-boys-basketball-fenwick-mike-smith-st-joseph-nick-rakocevik-tl-0204-20160201-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=February 1, 2016}} He was a four-year [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball starter at [[Fenwick High School (Oak Park, Illinois)|Fenwick High School]] in [[Oak Park, Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Everson |first1=Jered |title=In first year, Mike Smith is light-years ahead |url=https://www.columbiaspectator.com/sports/2017/03/02/in-first-year-mike-smith-is-light-years-ahead/ |website=[[Columbia Daily Spectator]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 2, 2017}} On January 18, 2016, as a senior, Smith scored a career-high 38 points in a 71–68 win over [[Simeon Career Academy]].{{cite web |last1=Helfgot |first1=Mike |title=Mike Smith leads No. 4 Fenwick past No. 3 Simeon 71-68 |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/high-school/ct-spt-0119-prep-bbk-simeon-fenwick-20160118-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=January 18, 2016}} Five days later, he scored 34 points against [[Riverside Brookfield High School]]. He led Fenwick to the [[Chicago Catholic League]] (CCL) championship, scoring a game-high 27 points against [[St. Joseph High School (Westchester, Illinois)|St. Joseph High School]] in the final.{{cite web |last1=Recchia |first1=Lauren |title=Fenwick shreds St. Joseph to win CCL title |url=https://www.rblandmark.com/News/Articles/2-23-2016/Fenwick-shreds-St.-Joseph-to-win-CCL-title/ |website=Riverside-Brookfield Landmark |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=February 23, 2016}} In his senior season, Smith averaged 19.3 points, 4.0 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game, helping his team to the Class 3A sectional final and a school-record 28 wins. He finished second in [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] voting to [[Charlie Moore (basketball)|Charlie Moore]] and left Fenwick with 1,800 career points, the second-most in school history behind [[Corey Maggette]].{{cite web |last1=Van Dril |first1=Eric |title=Boys basketball player of the year: Mike Smith |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/evanston/sports/ct-oak-mike-smith-player-of-the-year-tl-0331-20160331-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 31, 2016}} He was named [[Pioneer Press]] All-Area player of the year and CCL player of the year.{{cite web |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Fenwick's Mike Smith commits to Columbia |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/preps-talk/fenwicks-mike-smith-commits-columbia-0 |publisher=[[NBC Sports]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 22, 2016}} On March 26, Smith committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia]] over [[Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball|Dartmouth]].{{cite web |last1=Narang |first1=Bob |title=Fenwick's Mike Smith commits to Columbia |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/river-forest/sports/ct-oak-mike-smith-columbia-fenwick-tl-0323-20160323-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 26, 2016}} He held offers from many other [[mid-major]] programs and was not rated by major recruiting services.{{cite web |last1=Helfgot |first1=Mike |title=Fenwick's Mike Smith standing tall |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/ct-spt-0807-prep-basketball-recruiting-notes-20150806-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=August 6, 2015}} Smith reopened his recruitment upon the departure of Columbia head coach [[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]] but was drawn back to program after a three-hour phone call with its new coach [[Jim Engles]]. ==College career== ===Columbia=== [[File:Mike Smith Brown v Columbia basketball game (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright=.7|Smith at [[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia]] in 2020]] On November 11, 2016, Smith made his collegiate debut for Columbia, scoring 14 points in a 73–66 win over [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook]].{{cite web |last1=Horn |first1=Austin |title=Men's basketball tops Stony Brook in season opener |url=https://www.columbiaspectator.com/sports/2016/11/11/mens-basketball-tops-stony-brook-season-opener/ |website=[[Columbia Daily Spectator]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=November 12, 2016}} He scored a freshman season-high 24 points in a 67–62 loss to [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]] on January 21, 2017. As a freshman, Smith averaged 13.6 points and 3.4 assists per game, starting in all 27 games, and set the program's single-season first-year scoring record with 368 points.{{cite web |title=Mike Smith |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/mike-smith/12617 |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020}} On December 10, he scored a sophomore season-high 28 points in a 73–68 loss to [[Navy Midshipmen men's basketball|Navy]].{{cite web |last1=Brett |first1=Alexander |last2=McDonough |first2=Ally |title=Men's basketball falls to Navy at home, 73-68 |url=https://www.columbiaspectator.com/sports/2017/12/11/mens-basketball-falls-to-navy-at-home-73-68/ |website=[[Columbia Daily Spectator]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=December 10, 2017}} He finished the season averaging 17.6 points, which led his team and ranked second in the [[Ivy League]], and a conference-high 4.6 assists per game. Smith collected second-team All-Ivy League and third-team All-Metropolitan honors.{{cite web |title=Mike Smith Earns Second Team All-Ivy League Status |url=https://www.nmnathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=9600&ATCLID=211704383 |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 6, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Mike Smith Adds Third Team All-Met To Resume |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/news/2018/4/23/211712763.aspx |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=April 23, 2018}} On November 16, 2018, his second game as a junior, he scored a then career-high 31 points in a 94–83 loss to [[Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball|Youngstown State]].{{cite web |title=Lions Iced By Penguins, 94-83 |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/news/2018/11/16/mens-basketball-lions-iced-by-penguins-94-83.aspx |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=November 17, 2018}} On December 2, Smith matched his career-high in scoring with 31 points and 5 steals in an 87–86 double [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss to [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware]].{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Zachary |title=Men's basketball loses double overtime thriller 87-86 to Delaware |url=https://www.columbiaspectator.com/sports/2018/12/03/mens-basketball-loses-double-overtime-thriller-87-86-to-delaware/ |website=[[Columbia Daily Spectator]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=December 3, 2018}} On December 12, it was announced that he would miss the remainder of the season with a [[Tear of meniscus|torn meniscus]] suffered five days earlier against [[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]].{{cite web |last1=Browne |first1=Rob |title=Columbia's Mike Smith out for season with torn meniscus |url=http://ivyhoopsonline.com/2018/12/14/report-columbias-mike-smith-out-for-season-with-torn-meniscus/ |publisher=Ivy Hoops Online |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=December 14, 2018}} In eight games, Smith averaged 15.8 points and 5 assists per game. Smith returned to action in his senior season debut on November 5, 2019, scoring 22 points in a 65–63 loss to [[Lafayette Leopards men's basketball|Lafayette]].{{cite web |title=Lafayette Holds Off Lions, 65-63, in Season Debut |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/news/2019/11/5/mens-basketball-lafayette-holds-off-lions-65-63-in-season-debut.aspx |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=November 5, 2019}} On February 15, 2020, he scored a career-high 38 points in a 77–73 double overtime loss to [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]]. It was the most points by a Columbia player in a single game since [[Buck Jenkins]] scored a school-record 47 points in 1991.{{cite web |title=Smith's Career Night Not Enough as Harvard Outlasts Lions, 77-73, in Double OT |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/news/2020/2/15/mens-basketball-smiths-career-night-not-enough-as-harvard-outlasts-lions-77-73-in-double-ot.aspx |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=February 15, 2020}} One week later, Smith scored 37 points in an 83–65 loss to [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]].{{cite web |title=Yale Sinks Columbia, 83-65 |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/news/2020/2/22/mens-basketball-yale-sinks-columbia-83-65.aspx |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=February 22, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged a conference-leading 22.8 points, 4.5 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game while being named to the second team All-Ivy League. In his senior season, Smith scored 684 points, the second-highest single-season total in program history, and averaged the most points for an Ivy League player since 1989.{{cite web |title=Mike Smith Named Second Team All-Ivy League |url=https://gocolumbialions.com/news/2020/3/11/mens-basketball-mike-smith-named-second-team-all-ivy-league.aspx |publisher=Columbia University Athletics |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 11, 2020}} ===Michigan=== [[File:Mike Smith Michigan (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Smith with the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] in 2020]] On April 10, 2020, Smith announced that he would graduate and transfer to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] for his final season. He was attracted to the program because of head coach [[Juwan Howard]].{{cite web |last1=Hawkins |first1=James |title=Michigan lands Columbia grad transfer Mike Smith, nation's No. 6 scorer |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2020/04/10/michigan-lands-columbia-grad-transfer-mike-smith-nations-no-6-scorer/5130623002/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=April 10, 2020}} Smith was ranked the 11th best graduate transfer according to ESPN and chose the Wolverines over offers from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]].{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=No. 11-ranked graduate transfer Mike Smith chooses Michigan |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29021286/no-11-ranked-graduate-transfer-mike-smith-chooses-michigan |accessdate=April 13, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 10, 2020}} In his debut for Michigan on November 25, Smith scored 16 points and had eight assists in a 96–82 win against [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]].{{cite news |title=No. 25 Michigan handles Bowling Green, 96-82 |url=https://www.thetelegram.com/sports/basketball/no-25-michigan-handles-bowling-green-96-82-524392/ |access-date=November 25, 2020 |work=[[The Telegram]] |date=November 25, 2020}} On March 7, 2021, Smith scored 11 points and seven assists in a 64–70 loss to [[2020–21 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. With his seven assists he surpassed 500 career assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401263325|title=Michigan State beats No. 2 Michigan 70-64, boosts NCAA hopes|access-date=March 7, 2021|date=March 7, 2021|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/7/mens-basketball-recap-at-michigan-state.aspx|title=Smith Reaches 500 Career Assists as Michigan Falls to MSU|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 7, 2021|date=March 7, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} On March 12, Michigan opened its [[2021 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] play with a 79–66 victory over [[2020–21 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] in the quarterfinals. Michigan was led by Smith with 18 points and set a Big Ten Tournament record with 15 assists.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/12/mens-basketball-recap-vs-maryland.aspx|title=Smith, Bench Help Michigan Overcome Slow Start Against Maryland|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 12, 2021|date=March 12, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} The record stood until [[Braden Smith (basketball)|Braden Smith]] posted 16 on March 12 in the [[2026 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] against [[2025–26 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7120656/2026/03/15/purdue-michigan-big-ten-championship-basketball-score-result/|title=Braden Smith, Purdue cap brilliant run through Big Ten tourney with upset of Michigan|accessdate=March 18, 2026|date=March 15, 2026|work=[[The Athletic]]|publisher=[[The New York Times]]|author=Dochterman, Scott}} He averaged 9 points and 5.3 assists per game, helping lead the team to the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament. On April 7, 2021, Smith declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing the additional season of eligibility the NCAA granted in light of the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2021/04/07/michigan-basketball-mike-smith-college-eligibility-nba-draft/7126452002/ |title=Michigan basketball's Mike Smith passes on extra year in college, declares for NBA draft |first=Orion |last=Sang |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=April 7, 2021 |access-date=April 7, 2021}} His 5.3 assists per game also led the Big Ten conference.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/mike-smith-9.html|title=Mike Smith|accessdate=March 7, 2024|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]}} ==Professional career== [[File:Майк Сміт.jpg|thumb|upright=.7|Smith in 2022 with [[Astoria Bydgoszcz]]]] ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Smith joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news |last1=Zuke |first1=Ryan |title=Michigan’s Mike Smith, Chaundee Brown find NBA homes as undrafted free agents |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2021/07/michigans-mike-smith-chaundee-brown-find-nba-homes-as-undrafted-free-agents.html |access-date=October 11, 2021 |work=[[MLive.com]] |date=July 30, 2021}} He was selected with the 13th pick of the second round of the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web |title=2021 NBA G League Draft averaged 9.1 points, 2.5 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Mike Smith is a newcomer at Saints
